sections.title: Plants, Water, Light, and Earth
sections.description: Starting with photosynthesis, the requisite water content of biological cells, the properties of water and dabbling in biochemistry, physics, geology, and meteorology, we will discuss how the relationship between plants, water and light has shaped the world around us. We will start ~3.5 billion years ago with the evolution of photosynthesis, and then jump quickly to ~440 million years ago with the onset of the great terraforming and climate changes that occurred because plants invaded land. We will then move forward in time while discussing how plants, and their incessant need for water and light, blindly shaped the journey to present day Earth. Through this progression, we will learn about changes in plant form and function focusing on how plants work, as well as the global-scale interactions between plant function and climate. We will be guided by both lay-science and primary literature, and we will interrogate older hypotheses for this Plant-Earth system with newer data/interpretations to see how science and knowledge progress. This will primarily be a reading and discussion seminar, but we will have a few ‘field trips’ to perform some simple lab demonstrations and examine plants in action (meaning when Spring has sprung, we will occasionally go outside). The course will be graded based on short worksheets and writing assignments performed largely during class, as well as demonstrated knowledge that the required reading material has been read prior to class.
